title: Game remakes and source-provenance discovery
summary: Add twelve qualified game remakes/source restorations and record evidence-based exclusions and duplicate derivatives.
notes: Root personally searched all six requested platform families and checked candidate roots, original source provenance and implementation. Twelve qualified source/remake additions; other reviewed roots recorded as duplicate derivatives, insufficient reconstruction evidence or game-specific emulation. No discovery worker used. No upstream program executed. Runtime and matching claims remain unverified. Pinned source bytes are temporary review inputs only; retained submission carries identities without embedded source excerpts.

sources.reason: Semantic JavaScript player, enemies and projectiles plus TMX screen maps reconstruct Exolon without a Z80 interpreter. Vitorc/outfit switching, ammunition, grenades and teleport state are implemented. Fidelity of timing and every screen is not independently established.

Recreates the bouncing-ball game through semantic movement, portals, water/buoy, magnet and launcher state. Configuration declares 75 screens and the tree contains TMX screen maps. Original timing parity is unverified.

Unity reconstruction uses original sprites and a 30 by 20 board decoder for boulders, diamonds, force fields, gravity, teleports and other objects. This is newly implemented gameplay rather than recovered Z80 code.

Substantial room/maze, player, projectile and enemy implementation. Author explicitly excludes accurate enemy AI from completion; inspected enemy movement uses common randomized placeholders for several distinct classes.

Recreates a three-dimensional character-map world, safe zones, rescue characters, grenades and ants in C#. Ant movement uses breadth-first path search with a distance cap; this is semantic replacement logic rather than recovered original AI.

Reconstructs the original BASIC political simulation as an engine plus console UI, including groups, monthly accounts, audiences, escape and assassination logic. Author says part of the revolution mechanic remains incomplete and graphics/effects differ.

New implementation of Frank N Stein and Rebooted variants, with JSON map types, skeleton pieces, springs, ice and poles. Current changelog has three maps and placeholder monsters; replacement graphics/music and timing changes are explicit.

Rewrites Barry Jones Jolly Roger through a prior BASIC/MasterBASIC remake into Solo Forth. Source and original graphics conversion utilities are present. Interface, logic and plot improvements are planned, so this is an unfinished reinterpretation, not matching original code.

Preserves the original Compute! Goblin BASIC listing alongside a refactored native C64 version. Uses direct screen/SID memory and reduces ROM character copying from 2048 bytes to the needed digit characters.

New-code chain-reaction strategy remake from published rules: cell thresholds use neighbor count, explosions transfer ownership, and last surviving color wins. Includes multiple CPU levels and optional network play. No original artwork or code is used.

Ghidra-to-NASM reconstruction names functions, sprite data and memory layout. Progress reports 3918 real mnemonics and 305 raw-byte instruction fallbacks to preserve original encodings; matching bytes do not prove every annotation correct. Inspected enemy code still has generic labels and some misleading shift comments.
GitHub fork of bertoom/OpenPlayerManager. Upstream inspected separately; do not create two entries for the same partial community remake.

Raw disk-section objdump and hardware-register annotations do not establish loaded game-code reconstruction. Script rounds requested 0x3ff00 offset down to 512-byte blocks while using 0x3ff00 VMA; source provenance cannot be assumed. Status documents placeholder gameplay and unresolved original mechanics; community assets do not prove a faithful port.

Whole-program C recompilation retains explicit emulated 8086 registers, segment memory and hardware runtime. Detailed oracle findings are useful, but this is game-specific emulation/recompilation rather than semantic native restoration; retain in audit backlog under user preference.
